# Dimension: Self-Hosting, Credential Management, Execution History

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Self-Hosting and Deployment

### Deployment Methods

| Method | Details | Source |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Docker Compose (full) | PostgreSQL + RabbitMQ + Engine + Dashboard + Migration | [3] |
| Hatchet Lite | Single container for dev/low-volume; "designed for development and low-volume use-cases" | [12] |
| Hatchet CLI | `hatchet server start` command | [12] |
| Kubernetes | Helm charts available | [1] |

### Infrastructure Dependencies

| Dependency | Required? | Details | Source |
|------------|-----------|---------|--------|
| PostgreSQL 15.6 | Yes | Durable source of truth for all state | [2][3] |
| RabbitMQ 3 | Optional | For higher throughput; Postgres-only mode works for <100 req/s | [2][3][24] |
| Redis | No | Not a dependency | [2] |

### Docker Compose Services

Six services in the full deployment [3]:

1. PostgreSQL 15.6 (port 5435)
2. RabbitMQ 3 (port 5673, management UI port 15673)
3. Migration service (database schema setup)
4. Setup-Config service (configuration and certificates)
5. Hatchet Engine (gRPC port 7077)
6. Hatchet Dashboard (port 8080)

Default credentials: `admin@example.com` / `Admin123!!` [3].

### Resource Requirements

| Configuration | Specs | Throughput | Source |
|---------------|-------|------------|--------|
| Baseline DB | 4 CPU, 8 GB RAM (m7g.2xlarge) | Hundreds of events/s | [16] |
| Engine instances | 2 replicas on c7i.4xlarge | — | [16] |
| Tested max | m7g.8xlarge (8 CPU) | Up to 10k events/s | [16] |

Performance at the baseline configuration [16]:

| Events/sec | DB CPU | Execution Latency |
|------------|--------|-------------------|
| 100 | 15% | ~40ms |
| 500 | 60% | ~48ms |
| 2000 | 83% | ~220ms |

### Single-Host Viability

Hatchet Lite is explicitly designed for single-host deployment [12]. The full
Docker Compose deployment also runs on a single host [3]. No Kubernetes
requirement [1][12].

### Podman Compatibility

No official Podman documentation or compatibility statement found in any source.
Docker Compose files use standard constructs that should work with
`podman-compose`, but this is not verified by the Hatchet team.

## Credential Management

### Encryption

Three encryption strategies available [13]:

| Strategy | Variables | Source |
|----------|-----------|--------|
| Local keys | SERVER_ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEYSET, JWT public/private keysets | [13] |
| File-based | Same keys as files on disk | [13] |
| Google Cloud KMS | CLOUDKMS_ENABLED, KEY_URI, CREDENTIALS_JSON | [13] |

### Worker Authentication

Workers authenticate via `HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN` environment variable [19].
Tokens are created in the dashboard ("Settings" → "API Tokens") or via CLI [3][19].

### Secrets Injection

Environment variables are "securely stored and encrypted at rest" and "injected
into your worker containers at runtime" [20]. Configuration through Hatchet UI,
CLI, or service configuration files — no container rebuilds needed [20].

`HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN` is "automatically set for your service and should not be
set in your environment variables" [20].

### Credential Isolation Model

The architecture provides separation between API callers and workers [2][19][20]:

1. API Server handles external triggers — callers need an API token but not
   worker credentials [2]
2. Workers authenticate separately via `HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN` [19]
3. Workflow inputs/outputs are stored in PostgreSQL; secrets in worker
   environment variables are not persisted in execution history [20]

This means an LLM/PA can trigger workflows via the API without accessing the
credentials used by workers — **the core credential isolation requirement is met**.

## Execution History and Debugging

### Data Persistence

All task executions are persisted in PostgreSQL with inputs, outputs, timestamps,
and status [1][6]. "Every task you invoke is durable — Hatchet persists it, its
state, and its results" [6].

### Per-Step Inspection

The web dashboard displays [25]:
- Input data per task
- Output data per task
- Duration per task
- Error details for failures
- Execution topology (DAG visualization)

Programmatic access to step outputs via `ctx.task_output(parent_task)` [23][25].

### Logging

| Feature | Details | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Log methods | context.log(), language-native loggers | [7][26] |
| Log line limit | 1000 lines per task | [7][26] |
| Log view | Built-in logging view in dashboard | [7] |
| Root logger | Recommended for multi-file workflows | [7] |

### Retention

| Setting | Default | Source |
|---------|---------|--------|
| SERVER_LIMITS_DEFAULT_TENANT_RETENTION_PERIOD | 720h (30 days) | [13] |
| SERVER_ENABLE_DATA_RETENTION | true | [13] |
| SERVER_LIMITS_DEFAULT_EVENT_LIMIT | 1000 | [13] |
| SERVER_LIMITS_DEFAULT_TASK_RUN_LIMIT | 2000 | [13] |

### Streaming

Tasks can stream data in real-time via `put_stream` method on the Context
object [14]. Consumers subscribe to the workflow run ID. Critical limitation:
"You must begin consuming the stream before any events are published. Any events
published before a consumer is initialized will be dropped" [14].

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No explicit Podman testing** — untested with Podman/podman-compose
- **1000 log line limit per task** — could be restrictive for verbose CLI output [7]
- **Idle resource footprint undocumented** — benchmarks show production load but
  not idle consumption for Hatchet Lite
- **4 MB payload limit** mentioned in discovery agent findings — limits data-heavy
  step outputs
- **Stream race condition** — consumers must subscribe before events are
  published [14]
